meta.vantage: github-hosted ubuntu runner to the ap-southeast-2 staging stack; budgets derived here are not comparable to numbers measured from any other vantage

queue-switch-first.note: budgetMs is baseline.maxMs times 1.25, rounded up to 25ms. That worst run is an outlier: 17 of the 19 landed between 279 and 414ms and the median max was 379ms. Ratchet target once the listing cache lands — this is the cache-miss arm.

queue-switch-subsequent.note: budgetMs is baseline.maxMs times 1.25, rounded up to 25ms. The soak spanned 252 to 406ms with a 337ms median max. Ratchet target once the listing cache lands — this is the cache-hit arm and should fall furthest.

tab-switch-first.note: budgetMs is baseline.maxMs times 1.25, rounded up to 25ms. The soak spanned 281 to 414ms with a 347ms median max. Cache-miss arm of the To-Read/Read switch.

tab-switch-subsequent.note: budgetMs is baseline.maxMs times 1.25, rounded up to 25ms. The soak spanned 264 to 398ms with a 347ms median max. Cache-hit arm of the To-Read/Read switch.

assign-to-queue.note: budgetMs is baseline.maxMs times 1.25, rounded up to 25ms. The soak spanned 564 to 715ms with a 647ms median max — the slowest operation, and the tightest spread of the seven. Ratchet target when the assign response becomes an out-of-band fragment instead of a full reader re-render.

open-article.note: budgetMs is baseline.maxMs times 1.25, rounded up to 25ms. The soak spanned 347 to 564ms with a 414ms median max. Ratchet target when visible cards are prefetched; expect responseStart to collapse on a prefetch hit.

back-to-queue.note: budgetMs is baseline.maxMs times 1.25, rounded up to 25ms. That worst run is an outlier: 18 of the 19 landed between 327 and 489ms and the median max was 402ms. Ratchet target when the reader exit becomes instant.
